chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: Wes Montgomery: first hearing and the Kenton Neophonic score
summary: Jones was stunned by Wes Montgomery's chordal playing and wrote a Neophonic work for him, mailing a guitar demo.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You , I know, have worked with Wes Montgomery, and we haven't talked about Wes at all.
Oh, yes, well that's a must. Well, the
first time I heard Wes play I didn't know whether to run or what, stand up and run. I'd never heard anybody play a guitar like that, you know? And --
You mentioned in the quotes in Stanley Dance's book that his approach was similar to your approach when you were playing guitar.

So that's one of the reasons -- in fact I did a thing here with Stan Kenton, the neophonic thing, and I wrote a big work for Wes. They had all the writers. I just had come out here to California, and I took a lot of time on this, and Stan has been trying to get that score ever since, but after Wes died I just got sentimental about it.
And put it in my files, you know?
But he didn't know -- he had to say on the road, and he didn't know the melodic lines that I was going to use on guitar, so what I did was to play it on guitar and mail it to him.
And when he came there he was ready. He
knew exactly what I had in mind, you know?
So I just played it on guitar and recorded it myself, you know. And --
